newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end weaker on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end weaker on profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-taking ended a winning streak in Kuala Lumpur shares from last week, with share prices selling down across-the-board.

Talk of a Cabinet reshuffling circulated in the market but did not have a definitive impact, dealers said. Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said late on Tuesday he has no plans to reshuffle his line-up of ministers.

"I suppose the rumours might have gotten people concerned," said an institutional dealer at a local brokerage firm. The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised shares ended down 4.58 points to 1,247.90, above its 1,245.18 session low.
News reports about the deteriorating health of Chinese premier leader Deng Xiaoping was largely ignored by the Malaysian market, dealers said.
"This market has its own momentum," said a dealer with a foreign securities firm. "Today, we see some profit-taking."
Market volume totalled 447 million shares, compared with 517 million on Monday. Losers outpaced gainers by 424 to 194.
Within the small-capitalisation sector, the Second Board index slipped 2.69 to 639.92.
